function_question: How does nature move through air and water quietly?

opening.text: There was a boy called Hugo who lived in Sunny Hills, in a house right next to a railway tunnel.
Hugo waved at the trains as they rushed in and out of the tunnel. He knew every timetable by heart.
A new high-speed train arrived. Every time it left the tunnel: BOOM! Windows rattled and the neighbours complained. "It's the shape of the nose," said the engineers.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: BOOM at the tunnel
chapters.line: Hugo hears the boom again and wonders: could a new nose make the train quiet?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Hugo asks for help
chapters.line: Hugo has lots of questions, and he needs a teammate. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Hugo go exploring to meet animals that glide through air and water quietly.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the long nose
chapters.line: The heroes share the secret they all use.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the splash lab
chapters.line: Every hero needs training. Hugo hands you clay, a tall glass and a ruler.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The why detective
chapters.line: Hugo asks: why does the train go BOOM? Then he asks why again…

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great train starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big test
chapters.line: The first nose makes a big splash. You fix it, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Just a whoosh
chapters.line: The new train glides out of the tunnel with just a whoosh.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. The BOOM is keeping Hugo's neighbours awake, and the train needs a quieter nose. Can you help him? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved this long ago. Tap each card to meet four nature heroes who move through air and water quietly!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which shape will make the smallest splash?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your train's nose from the side and from above, like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build three noses and let's see which one makes the smallest splash!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, the Sunny Hills train wears YOUR nose. It glides out of the tunnel with a gentle whoosh, and Hugo's neighbours sleep soundly!

quick_check.question: A real train with a kingfisher-shaped nose used about 15% less electricity. If the old train used 100 units, how many does the new one use?
quick_check.right: Right! 100 take away 15 is 85. A nature idea that's quieter AND saves energy!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Less electricity means take away: try 100 − 15.

clue_cards.name: Kingfisher
clue_cards.does: Dives from air into water with almost no splash.

clue_cards.name: Dolphin
clue_cards.trick: A smooth, rounded head and body.
clue_cards.does: Water flows past with very little resistance.

clue_cards.name: Owl
clue_cards.trick: Comb-like fringes on the front edge of its wings.
clue_cards.does: Break up air swirls, so it flies almost silently.

clue_cards.name: Shark
clue_cards.trick: Skin covered in tiny tooth-shaped scales.

predict.prompt: Big splash or small splash? Predict first!
predict.explain: A long, slowly widening shape pushes the water aside bit by bit. Blunt shapes shove it all at once, so it splashes up high.

lab.title: The splash lab
lab.predict: Which shape will make the smallest splash?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: 5 Whys is a detective tool. You ask "why?" again and again until you find the root cause, the real problem hiding underneath. Today you'll use all 5 whys.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🪴 Why is the plant droopy? Its soil is bone dry.
parts.starter: Why does the train go BOOM? Because…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.example: 🪴 Why is the soil dry? The water dries up really fast.
parts.starter: Why does the air burst out of the tunnel? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🪴 Why so fast? The pot sits on a sunny windowsill.
parts.starter: Why is the air squeezed so hard? Because…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.what: Keep digging: don't stop at the easy answer.
parts.example: 🪴 Why is that a problem? The sun bakes the pot all afternoon.
parts.starter: Why is the air pushed all at once? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Reach the root cause, then fix that.
parts.example: 🪴 Root cause: too much sun. Move it to a shadier spot!
parts.starter: Why is the nose that shape? Because…

sketch_checklist: I drew the nose from the side and from above.
I added arrows showing how the air moves around it.
I marked where the driver's cab goes.

test.check_question: Is there still room for a driver in your best nose?

reflection.question: Which nature hero inspired your train's nose?
